name: Xi Yu
title: Assistant Professor; AMASS Laboratory
department: School of Manufacturing Systems and Networks
fitReason: Direct learned high-level coordination for real marine robots, alongside a broader multi-agent control and underactuated-robot program.

physicalEvidence.summary: May 2026 MCAPS trains transformer-based actor/critic coordination with PPO in VMAS, then runs policy inference on a shore laptop at Fern Ridge Lake, Oregon. A Platypus Lutra USV and BlueROV execute locally planned trajectories under learned specialization vectors. The field study reports one successful trial each of MCAPS and a greedy baseline; ROV communication is tethered Ethernet and USV uses short-range Wi-Fi without observed loss. GPS/USBL localization and recoverable open-water operation do not validate under-ice navigation or acoustic communications. This is real hierarchical learned coordination, not end-to-end learned low-level control. Yu and her advised coauthor contribute methods/investigation, but the deployment is collaborative offsite and current ASU access to those exact robots is unverified. March 2026 topology reconfiguration is simulation-only.

shortVisit.summary: Current AMASS recruiting distinguishes PhD admissions and projects for ASU-enrolled master’s students. A dated SURI 2026 listing offers underactuated-blimp hardware/control work to US and non-US students, but no current applicable external-master summer 2027 invitation is established.
